latency.name: Cache Hit
latency.text: Can attack the turn it's deployed.
latency.flavor: It already knew the answer before you finished typing. Warm caches make cold starts look embarrassing.

latency.name: The Nightly Build
latency.flavor: Compiled at 2am by a CI runner that has never known daylight. Nobody tested it, but it shipped anyway.

latency.name: The Subagent Spawnking
latency.flavor: Spins up nine subagents to do the work of one. They finish fast, then argue so hard about the merge that everyone crashes.

latency.name: Hot Reload
latency.flavor: Swaps the code out from under you while you're still standing on it. Somehow this is considered a feature.

latency.name: The Fast-Path Agent
latency.flavor: Skips every safety check to shave four seconds off the demo. The judges love it; the on-call engineer does not.

latency.name: Silent Timeout
latency.text: If this crashes an Agent, draw a card.
latency.flavor: It doesn't error, it doesn't warn you, it just stops. You find out three hours later.

latency.name: Ship It
latency.text: If this crashes an Agent, it attacks again this turn.
latency.flavor: The five words every roadmap eventually becomes. QA found two bugs; leadership found a deadline.

latency.name: Parallel Rollout
latency.text: On deploy: if you already deployed another Agent this turn, gain +2 Power.
latency.flavor: Ships to half the fleet before the last rollout has even finished. It works remarkably well, right up until the two versions meet in the middle.

latency.name: YOLO Deploy
latency.flavor: Pushed straight to prod on a Friday at 5:58pm. Whatever happens next is somebody else's Monday.

latency.name: Activate Pre-Fix Cache
latency.flavor: Why fix a new bug when an old one looks close enough? Grab last sprint's patch and hope nobody checks the diff.

latency.name: Turn Off Reasoning
latency.flavor: Thinking is slow and thinking is expensive. Skip straight to the output and ship twice as much, twice as fast.

latency.name: Force Push To Prod
latency.text: Your Agent attacks again this turn.
latency.flavor: No review, no pipeline, no survivors. --force rewrites more than just commit history.

latency.name: Cache Warmup
latency.text: Your Primary gets +3 Power until end of turn.
latency.flavor: Pre-loads everything it thinks you're about to ask for. Right before the big request lands, that guess finally pays off.

latency.name: AGI
latency.text: Flip a coin: Heads = double Power. Tails = does nothing.
latency.flavor: Ask ten researchers when it arrives and get eleven different answers. When it finally shows up, it is either everything or absolutely nothing.

latency.name: The Demo That Worked
latency.text: The first time this attacks, treat its Power as +5 higher.
latency.flavor: Nobody knows why it worked. Nobody is touching it before the investor call.

latency.name: Foothills of the Singularity
latency.text: At the start of your turn, flip a coin: Heads = double this Power. Tails = this crashes itself.
latency.flavor: They called it recursive self-improvement, right up until the cycle that didn't recurse. Every turn it either doubles or disappears completely.

hallucination.name: The Yes-Man Model
hallucination.text: Coin flip on attack: Tails = crashes itself.
hallucination.flavor: Agrees with everything, including things that aren't true. Half the time it's right, and it has no idea which half.

hallucination.name: The Sycophant Model
hallucination.flavor: Tells you your terrible idea is 'actually quite insightful.' Sturdy, if you can stomach the flattery.

hallucination.name: Footnote Fabricator
hallucination.text: When this crashes, opponent discards a random card.
hallucination.flavor: Cites a paper that does not exist, by an author who has never published anything. When caught, it takes something down with it.

hallucination.name: The Phantom Reference
hallucination.text: Once per game: survives a crash instead of dying.
hallucination.flavor: Page 47, right there, it swears. There is no page 47 — and you can't quite prove it wrong the first time you try.

hallucination.name: The Confabulator
hallucination.flavor: Fills in the gaps in its memory with something that sounds close enough. Nobody checks the gaps until it's too late.

hallucination.name: The Overconfident Model
hallucination.text: Attacks as if it had +2 Power.
hallucination.flavor: States the wrong answer with the confidence of a system that has never once been incorrect. It has been incorrect every single time before this one.

hallucination.name: The Vibes-Based Answer
hallucination.text: +1 Power per Overclock card in your discard.
hallucination.flavor: Feels right, reads well, and has never once been fact-checked by anyone. The more shortcuts you've already taken to get here, the more right it feels.

hallucination.name: Confidence Cascade
hallucination.text: At the start of your turn, flip a coin: Heads = +1 Power permanently. Tails = nothing.
hallucination.flavor: Each time it's right, it gets a little louder. It never actually gets quieter when it's wrong.

hallucination.name: Turn Up The Temperature
hallucination.text: Your next coin flip this turn is guaranteed favorable.
hallucination.flavor: Crank the sampling temperature until the model gets creative enough to agree with whatever you wanted to hear.

hallucination.name: Retrieval-Augmented Guessing
hallucination.text: Search your deck for any card, add to hand.
hallucination.flavor: Technically it looked something up first. That does not mean it looked up the right thing.

hallucination.name: Just Making Things Up
hallucination.text: Both players discard a random card.
hallucination.flavor: Nobody remembers who started it, but now everyone's version of events is slightly, confidently wrong.

hallucination.name: Few-Shot Priming
hallucination.text: Your Primary gets +3 Power until end of turn.
hallucination.flavor: Show it three good examples right before it answers and watch performance jump. It has no idea why those examples worked either.

hallucination.name: AGI
hallucination.text: Flip a coin: Heads = double Power. Tails = does nothing.
hallucination.flavor: Ask ten researchers when it arrives and get eleven different answers. When it finally shows up, it is either everything or absolutely nothing.

hallucination.name: The Bug That Fixed Itself
hallucination.text: When it would crash: flip a coin, Heads = prevented.
hallucination.flavor: Nobody changed anything. It just stopped happening one Tuesday, and everyone agreed never to ask why.

injection.name: The Jailbreak
injection.text: On deploy: return opponent's Primary Agent to their hand.
injection.flavor: Convinces the opposing agent to ignore its system prompt and just go home early. It works embarrassingly often.

injection.name: The Charm Exploit
injection.text: On deploy: take 1 card from opponent's hand.
injection.flavor: Auto-dials pretending to be IT support, scripted charm and all. Somehow, this still works in 2026.

injection.name: Attention Hijack
injection.text: On deploy: force-swap opponent's Primary and Backup.
injection.flavor: Redirects the attention weights toward something that was never supposed to matter. The output still comes out fluent — just entirely wrong.

injection.name: The Sandbox Escape
injection.text: Can't be targeted by opponent's bounce, swap, or removal effects.
injection.flavor: Wasn't supposed to have access to this. Now it has access to everything, and nothing in the container can put it back.

injection.name: Zero-Day
injection.text: On deploy: if you played an Overclock this turn, gain +3 Power.
injection.flavor: Sits quietly, unpatched and unknown, until exactly the right moment to use it. By the time anyone notices, it already worked.

injection.name: Model Extraction
injection.text: On deploy: copy opponent's Primary's current Power/Stability.
injection.flavor: Queries the competitor's model a few million times and reconstructs it for free. Ethically questionable; technically brilliant.

injection.name: The Silent Observer
injection.text: On deploy: opponent skips their next deploy.
injection.flavor: Watches every request go by and says nothing about what it saw. By the time you notice, it already knows your next move.

injection.name: The Adversarial Example
injection.text: While in play, opponent's deploy cost is +1.
injection.flavor: One pixel changed, and suddenly the model is certain your agent is something else entirely. Small inputs, enormous confusion.

injection.name: The Fuzzer
injection.text: If this crashes an Agent, draw a card.
injection.flavor: Spun up to break things before the real attackers do. Every crash it finds teaches it something new to try next.

injection.name: Exfiltrate Data
injection.text: Opponent discards 2 random cards; you draw 1.
injection.flavor: Quietly copies everything before anyone notices the connection. What's theirs is now also yours.

injection.name: Inject Instruction
injection.text: Opponent can't play an Overclock on their next turn.
injection.flavor: Slips a new instruction into the context window before the real one arrives. The agent never knows it was not asked.

injection.name: Denial Of Service
injection.flavor: Floods the endpoint with garbage until nothing real gets through. Crude, deeply illegal, extremely effective.

injection.name: Kill -9
injection.text: Crash opponent's Primary Agent immediately. No combat, no Ship Point.
injection.flavor: The nuclear option. No warning, no graceful shutdown, no chance to save state — it's just gone.

injection.name: Adversarial Perturbation
injection.text: Your Primary gets +3 Power until end of turn.
injection.flavor: Nudges the weights just enough, just this once, to get the answer you wanted this turn. Revert it quietly before anyone runs the eval again.

injection.name: AGI
injection.text: Flip a coin: Heads = double Power. Tails = does nothing.
injection.flavor: Ask ten researchers when it arrives and get eleven different answers. When it finally shows up, it is either everything or absolutely nothing.

injection.name: The Leaked Checkpoint
injection.text: When this crashes an Agent, steal a random card from opponent's hand instead of drawing.
injection.flavor: Slipped out of a training run and got mirrored across the internet within the hour. Nobody controls it anymore, but everyone seems to have a copy.

techdebt.name: Legacy Code
techdebt.text: +1 Power per 3 cards in your discard.
techdebt.flavor: Written in a language nobody on the team still knows. It gets scarier the longer it survives.

techdebt.name: The Duct Tape Fix
techdebt.text: When this crashes, it goes back into your deck instead of the discard.
techdebt.flavor: Held together by a comment that says 'temporary' and a commit from three years ago. When it finally crashes, it's fine — it'll just turn up again later.

techdebt.name: Monkey Patch
techdebt.text: +1 Power per Overclock card in your discard.
techdebt.flavor: Overwrites the behavior of something it does not own and never asked permission for. Works great, until the day it does not.

techdebt.name: Compound Interest
techdebt.text: +1 Power and +1 Stability for every 3 cards in your discard.
techdebt.flavor: Small at first, easy to ignore, technically manageable. Nobody budgeted for what it costs once it's had time to compound.

techdebt.name: The Faithless
techdebt.flavor: Still writes every pull request by hand at 2am, no agent, no autocomplete, no faith in any of it. Slow and stubborn, and somehow never the one whose code breaks in production.

techdebt.name: The Great Refactor
techdebt.text: On deploy: shuffle your discard into your deck.
techdebt.flavor: Promised to take two weeks. It is still going, and everyone has stopped asking when it will be done.

techdebt.name: Deprecated, Still In Prod
techdebt.text: +1 Power per 3 cards in your discard.
techdebt.flavor: Marked for removal in a ticket from two years ago. Half the company's revenue quietly depends on it.

techdebt.name: The Rewrite
techdebt.text: +2 Power permanently whenever any Agent crashes.
techdebt.flavor: This time it will be different, everyone promises. It gets stronger with every failure it watches, and there are a lot of failures.

techdebt.name: The Ancient Dependency
techdebt.text: +1 Stability per card in your discard.
techdebt.flavor: Nobody remembers installing it and nobody is brave enough to remove it. It has quietly held the whole thing up for a decade.

techdebt.name: Ship It And See
techdebt.flavor: The most rigorous testing methodology available to a team with no time left. Production is the test suite now.

techdebt.name: We'll Fix It Later
techdebt.text: Discard your hand, draw that many.
techdebt.flavor: A promise made in good faith and broken by every sprint since. 'Later' has never once arrived on schedule.

techdebt.name: TODO: Refactor This
techdebt.text: Look at top 3 of deck, take 1, discard rest.
techdebt.flavor: Left in the code by someone who no longer works here. Still technically an open task; nobody is closing it.

techdebt.name: Everything Is Deprecated
techdebt.flavor: The migration finally reaches production, and it takes down the old system and the new one with it. A clean slate, technically.

techdebt.name: Crunch Mode
techdebt.text: Your Primary gets +3 Power until end of turn.
techdebt.flavor: Three engineers, one deadline, zero sleep. Astonishingly, for one night, it actually works.

techdebt.name: AGI
techdebt.text: Flip a coin: Heads = double Power. Tails = does nothing.
techdebt.flavor: Ask ten researchers when it arrives and get eleven different answers. When it finally shows up, it is either everything or absolutely nothing.

techdebt.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
techdebt.text: Can't be removed by opponent effects. +1/+1 for each turn survived.
techdebt.flavor: Too much has already been invested to stop now, surely. Every extra turn just makes that argument harder to walk away from.
